format.decision: human-decisions.md item 8: context before the question. The minimal reading is taken: only the question moves. Task and route stay before the context, so N questions with one task over one context share every byte through <|qd_context_end|>.
format.version_marker: a new structural marker M_FORMAT = '<|qd_prompt_format|>' (shape <|qd_...|>, so the one escape rule covers it) and PROMPT_FORMAT = 2 in both renderers, added to MARKERS in both; a v4 prompt has no such line. The wire schema_version stays 1: callers send the same requests.

refusal_both_ways.serving: crates/qd-runtime/src/release.rs: MANIFEST_FORMAT 'qd-release.v1' -> 'qd-release.v2' and expected_identity.prompt_format required and equal to render::PROMPT_FORMAT. A v5 runtime refuses every v4 release (no prompt_format, v1 format); a v4-era runtime refuses a v5 release by format. qd-export writes prompt_format read from the checkpoint's recipe (absent = 1), never the current constant, so a v4 checkpoint exported after the change is stamped 1 and refused, not mislabelled.
refusal_both_ways.training: python/qd_train/artifacts.py ShardHeader.prompt_format, serialized only when != 1 so v4 header hashes do not move (the span_collapse_policy precedent, GAP-V4-TRAIN-HEADER-OMITS-SPAN-COLLAPSE-POLICY); the shard reader refuses a header whose prompt_format differs from render.PROMPT_FORMAT. The qd_data code fingerprint in every shard header (render.py is in it) already refuses v4 shards under v5 code.

format.prefix_sharing: Within one request nothing changes for qd-metal: the rendered prefix still ends where the slot suffixes begin (now with the question as its last line), every slot and its deranged pass continue read-only from that one snapshot (crates/qd-metal/src/model.rs:34-39), and no qd-metal file changes for v5. Across questions over one context the bytes through <|qd_context_end|>\n become identical, so a serving lane can snapshot there and run each question as part of its slots' continuations (question line + slot suffix, tens of tokens recomputed per continuation; no concat_kv copy, which would cost ~24 KB per prefix position per question [I]). That needs a shared-prefix offset on RenderedPrompt, a snapshot cache keyed by its digest and a tokenization-additivity test at the new split (the '|>\n' | '<|qd_question|>' boundary is the same class as today's prefix|suffix boundary [I]). It is post-v5 serving work (GAP-RT-QUESTION-BEFORE-CONTEXT-BLOCKS-CROSS-QUESTION-PREFIX-CACHE-2026-10-02 keeps its serving half) and waits for the foreign qd-metal/qd-runtime edits to land.
format.expected_cost_report_only: The span pointer scores line-start hidden states. Under causal attention those states no longer see the question (GAP-V5-CONTEXT-FIRST-LINE-STARTS-DO-NOT-SEE-THE-QUESTION-2026-10-02). qa.answer_span and the needle suite are the span consumers; val_top1.span may fall. Report-only, no kill criterion; it is one reason v5 is never read against F.

arm_noul_weight.what: v5's recipe plus --noul-weight 4, seeds 0, 1, 2, after J5'.
arm_noul_weight.flag: --noul-weight w multiplies the cross-entropy at every supervised letter position whose target is the noul letter (Z), in every family; the letter loss stays a mean over supervised positions (sum of w_i * ce_i over the count of supervised positions), so w is a pure multiplier on a Z-gold row's pull and every other row's pull is unchanged; the span channel's abstain row is not weighted. New code in python/qd_train/fused_ce.py (a per-position weight) and python/qd_train/backbone.py (_letter_loss); recipe key noul_weight recorded only when given; refused with w <= 0 or non-finite.

w.why: Fable's range is 3-5. v5 carries 6,010 prose-noul rows against the 22,624 MMLU/CSQA letter rows they compete with after E_val's exclusions (v5_accounting.json): parity needs w >= 22,624 / 6,010 = 3.76. 4 is the smallest value in the range that reaches parity (24,040 vs 22,624); 3 stays below it (18,030); 5 adds in-distribution risk with no parity argument. On question form alone (~3,604 rows) w = 4 gives 14,416 vs 22,624.

arm_noul_weight.arm_rows: the arm's three ft rows (seeds 0, 1, 2) and each one's one completed epoch-score-val eval row, from the arm ledger only; a second eval row for an arm ft row refuses.

arm_noul_weight.confounds: Only the loss weight differs from v5, seed for seed; kernels are non-deterministic, so pairs are not bit-identical and the comparison is seed counts and envelopes, never per-seed pairs.

comparison.targets_form: seed_holds. A seed holds a category iff its count is at least half: 2 * n >= n_total (>= 30/60, the F2 bar of campaign/v4-noul-v3b-preregistered.json). A target clears iff all three arm seeds hold AND the arm holds on strictly more seeds than v5's envelope does.
comparison.room: a target has room iff v5 holds on at most 2 of its 3 seeds; with 3 of 3 it cannot clear (cannot_clear). Decided from the envelope alone, before the arm's rows are read. If exactly one target has no room it is read as a guard instead (the arm must hold on 3 of 3 seeds too) and the decision rests on the other target; if neither has room the arm does not launch (launch_condition), and any rows that exist anyway read 'refused'.
comparison.guards_form: strict envelope, as campaign/f-successor-preregistered.json comparison.guard_loses, with the arm's worst seed as the candidate: higher-better loses iff the arm's minimum < v5's minimum; lower-better loses iff the arm's maximum > v5's maximum; ties never lose. Counts on the integers n / n_total by i128 cross-multiplication (the float only cross-checked); ECE on the recorded f64.

outcomes.wins: every target with room clears and no guard (including the absolute guard and any no-room target read as a guard) loses. Feeds the next re-plan only.
outcomes.quiet: every required row and metric was read, at least one target had room, and the arm does not win.
outcomes.refused: a required row is missing, doubled or not completed; a required metric is absent or not run; a recorded value disagrees with its own counts; an identity or comparability check fails; or no target has room. Never quiet.

It exists before the arm's rows are read; the binding JSON wins any disagreement and a disagreement refuses.

NEEDLE_MIN_RECALL 0.95, NEEDLE_CASES_PER_DEPTH 60, NEEDLE_TARGET_TOKENS 8192 and the hit rule are unchanged (python/qd_train/needle.py:386-393); no agent moves them (rule 2).
gate_suite_change.today: build_suite sizes by len(text) // 3 (python/qd_train/needle.py:210-218, :254); the eval row's needle_suite_tokens is the real encoded span-sequence length (tools/real_ft_run.py:4674, :4805-4813): F seed 0 300 cases, median 8,473 (f4feac15).

readings.status: The lane's readings where the rulings leave a choice. Fable may strike or amend any of them in review; after the rename, Fable or the human may amend by commit before v5 seed 0's ft row's written_at.
readings.R1_needle_real_tokens: '8,192 real tokens' is read as the quantity the eval row already records: every case's encoded span sequence (prompt plus span-slot suffix, the real Qwen tokenizer, v5's format) is at most 8,192 tokens, grown by whole filler hunks while the next would still fit, so each case lands in (8,192 - largest filler hunk, 8,192]. The needle is inserted before measuring.
readings.R2_length_controls: the 1K/2K/4K length controls (report-only since F) are resized by the same real-token rule, so every needle length in v5 means real tokens. They are not comparable to F's controls.
readings.R3_prose_noul_counts: 2,000 own-repo + 2,000 contrast rows (floor 1,500 each after exclusions) is the lane's split of Fable's '>= 3,000, question form favoured' under the human's 'Both'. If either route falls below its floor after containment, the build refuses rather than topping up from the other route.
readings.R4_lower_layers: beyond C3, v5 also drops the lower-layer flags iff J6(f) holds prose (>= 30/60) AND fewer than half of the with-flag v4 seeds run (F seeds 0-2, plus 3-4 if run) hold prose. Otherwise kept: Fable's 2-of-3 vs 0-of-3 table leans keep.
readings.R5_noul_weight_scope: the weight applies to Z-gold letter positions in every family, as Fable wrote 'on Z-gold letter rows'; CLINC's 3,648 Z-gold rows are weighted too, which is why the pooled in-distribution abstention is a guard.
readings.R6_arm_form: seed_holds for the targets and the arm's worst seed for the guards are the lane's adaptation of the one-seed j6a/j6g form to three seeds per side; Fable may replace it.

build_order: 0. Prerequisites: L-prep merged (containment, attestation v2, --exclude-identity-keys); L-j6g's checker subcommand merged; the last v4 readers on main done (format.freeze).

1. The v5 build commit on main: the python/qd_data edits (render.py, general.py, mixture.py, sources.py, defect_class.py), the Rust renderer, release and export changes, needle.py, the noul-v3c and own-prose-v1 and composed-v2 manifests.

2. Build on the Mac (CPU): tools/real_tokenizer_pipeline.py with v5's argv (--max-seq-len 10240, --defect-class composed-v2, --defect-noul defect-noul-v3c, --general-record a0841f0d..., --general-max-rows 200000, --vocab full, --val-shards, --span-collapse-policy refuse-gold, --no-repo-history, --rev <build commit>).
3. Decontam: qd-prep containment over the rendered rows (L-prep's request form); exclusions.txt; rebuild with --exclude-identity-keys.
4. Attestation: v2 clean on enforced targets; the build's ledger row (ledger/mac-v5-shards-<date>.jsonl) records exclusions_sha256 and the attestation's sha256.
5. Mac prelude (j6g_prelude_mac.py's form) on the real v5 plan: PRELUDE OK, batches and widths, the noul-weight position count, the permutation line iff C1.

6. rsync to the box: shards/train, shards/val, data/pool/{train,val}.json, the corpora examples; never data/heldout/heldout.json and never the containment request or its pair list (both carry held-out text; rule 3).
7. Box queue after j6g -> STOP, on the human's yes: v5 s0-s2 -> seeds 3-4 iff spread -> J5' x3 -> noul-weight x3.
binds_iff: after Fable's review is applied and the file is renamed to campaign/v5-preregistered.json on main, before the written_at of v5 seed 0's ft row; the noul-weight arm's block binds before the written_at of the arm's first eval row.
